title: Permanent Migration Triggers (Zero-Downtime Trigger Fossil)
damaged_code:
```sql
-- SQL trigger used to sync old schema writes to the new schema during expansion phase
CREATE TRIGGER sync_old_to_new_user
AFTER INSERT ON users
FOR EACH ROW
BEGIN
    INSERT INTO user_profiles(user_id, bio) VALUES (NEW.id, NEW.bio);
END;
```
pattern: Database write-mirroring triggers left in production long after a zero-downtime deployment is complete and all application servers are upgraded to the new schema.
why_bad: Implicit mutation and performance drain. Triggers execute silently database-side, dramatically slowing down write transactions, creating lock contention, obscuring data lineage, and preventing the cleanup and drop of deprecated tables/columns.
detection:
The linter must observe:
1. A database schema with write triggers designed to sync data between two overlapping tables or columns.
2. The trigger's associated deprecated schema table/column has been unreferenced by active application nodes for days or weeks.
counterexample:
`Context-dependent`
```sql
-- Valid: Temporary trigger active strictly during a rolling upgrade window
```
strength: Contextual` (Requires DB catalog analysis and active application schema tracing)
